question: Name two optional pavement-marking features explicitly labeled in Figure 3D-1 at the roundabout.
model_answer: Direct Answer: Figure 3D-1 explicitly labels two optional pavement-marking features: (1) "Optional white diagonal markings" on the approach splitter area, and (2) an "Optional" yellow edge line around the inner (left-hand) edge of the circulatory roadway. Both are permitted (Option) treatments, not requirements. Options (permitted): - "A yellow edge line may be placed around the inner (left-hand) edge of the circulatory roadway (see Figure 3D-1) and may be used to channelize traffic." - "Channelizing lines... and chevron and diagonal markings... may be used on the approaches to and within the circulatory roadway of multi-lane roundabouts to separate traffic lanes, discourage lane changing, and/or compensate for off-tracking of larger trucks and vehicles." - YIELD (word) pavement markings, also shown in Figure 3D-1, "may be used on approaches to roundabouts." Visual evidence: [Image 1] Figure 3D-1 shows a callout reading "Optional white diagonal markings" pointing to the white hatched area near an approach, and an "Optional" callout with an arrow pointing to the yellow line at the inner edge of the circulatory roadway (a second "Optional" callout points to the YIELD word/triangle markings). [Image 2] is the full-page view of Figure 3D-1 on page 596, confirming the same "Optional white diagonal markings" and "Optional" labels. [Image 4] (Figure 3D-3, Sheet 1) similarly labels "Optional white diagonal markings" at a two-lane roundabout. [Image 5] (Figure 3D-3, Sheet 2) labels "Optional yellow edge line and diagonal yellow markings" used to extend the central island. [Image 3] (Figure 3D-8) shows related optional chevron and diagonal markings at roundabout ramp terminals but is not Figure 3D-1. Citations: - Section 3D.03 Option §4 (p.605) - Section 3D.02 Option §5 (p.595) - Section 3D.05 Option §1 (p.605) - Section 3D.01 Support §4 (p.595) - Figure 3D-1 (p.596)
gold_answer: Optional diagonal markings in the splitter island and an optional wide dotted extension of the circulatory roadway edge line.
